citations.anchor: lets the later Tailwind class win a conflict
citations.why: Pins the tailwind-merge half — `cn('px-4','px-8')` resolves to `px-8`, so the argument written last wins a conflict. The other half — that every component actually passes the caller's `className` last into `cn` — is now pinned by `library-conventions.spec.ts` → "passes the caller className last into every cn call", which parses all 161 `cn(...)` call sites and fails on any that takes a bare `className` anywhere but last.

citations.anchor: renders nothing for an empty errors array
citations.why: `FieldError` with `errors={[]}` renders an empty container (`container.innerHTML === ''`), so no `role="alert"` is opened; the sibling cases cover no-children-no-errors and message-less entries.

citations.anchor: still renders a supplied error when invalid={false} is passed
citations.why: Asserts `getByRole('alert').textContent === 'Nope'` with `invalid={false}` alongside `error`, so `invalid` cannot suppress the message.

citations.anchor: describes the control with the hint and the error, hint first
citations.why: Asserts `aria-describedby === 'email-description email-error'`, so neither the hint nor the error is lost from the assembly.

citations.anchor: appends a consumer aria-describedby rather than replacing it
citations.why: Asserts `aria-describedby === 'email-error extra-hint'`, so the caller-supplied value survives alongside the generated ids — the third clause of the invariant.

citations.anchor: makes the scroll container a tab stop once it overflows
citations.why: Asserts `tabindex` is absent before overflow is simulated and `'0'` after; the paired `adds no tab stop to a table that fits` case pins the 'only on actual overflow' direction.

citations.anchor: names the scroll region from the table it wraps
citations.why: Asserts `role === 'group'` and `aria-label === 'Members'` together on overflow, while `adds no tab stop to a table that fits` asserts `role` is null — the role and the name are set exclusively together.

citations.anchor: keeps the scrollport a visibly-focusable tab stop
citations.why: Asserts `tabindex === '0'` and that the class list carries `focus-visible:ring-2` and `focus-visible:ring-inset` on `[data-slot="sidebar-inset-scroll"]` — all three clauses. The `inset` assertion was added in the coverage sweep; the scrollport is the page body's clipping context, so an outset ring is painted outside its own overflow and never seen.

citations.anchor: exposes exactly one landmark of its own
citations.why: `getAllByRole('main')` has length 1 for a mounted `SidebarInset`, pinning the `<main>` clause. The enumeration of the rest is now pinned library-wide by `library-conventions.spec.ts` → "adds no landmark beyond the four it documents" (the only landmark *roles* declared anywhere in `src/` are `complementary` and `navigation` — `region` in particular is used nowhere) and "creates its landmark elements in four files and no others" (`<main>` only in `sidebar.tsx`/`app-loader.tsx`, `<nav>` only in breadcrumb/pagination/tab-nav).

citations.anchor: expect(wrapper.getAttribute('role')).toBe('group')
citations.why: The one nameable scroll container in the library is asserted to take `role="group"`, not `region` — the 'group, not region' clause, for the `Table` wrapper only.

citations.anchor: takes the collapsed panel out of the tab order and the a11y tree
citations.why: After collapsing, asserts the sidebar container has `inert` and `aria-hidden="true"` — both halves of the invariant.

citations.anchor: leaves Ctrl+B alone inside a text field
citations.why: Asserts the sidebar stays expanded and `fireEvent.keyDown` returns true (no `preventDefault`) with focus in an `Input`; sibling cases cover `textarea`, `select` and `contenteditable` — all four elements the invariant names. The `select` case was added in the coverage sweep.

citations.anchor: reports mobile on the very first frame, before any effect runs
citations.why: Records every rendered value and asserts `frames[0] === true` at a 500px viewport, so an effect-initialised `undefined` first frame fails.

citations.anchor: treats exactly 768px as desktop
citations.why: Asserts `useIsMobile()` is `false` at exactly 768px, with neighbouring cases at 500 and 1024 — the single breakpoint and its inclusive boundary.

citations.anchor: renders and still repaints when storage throws
citations.why: `localStorage.getItem`/`setItem` are stubbed to throw and the provider still applies the `dark` class — the localStorage clause: only persistence is lost.

citations.anchor: keeps toggling when the cookie jar is unwritable
citations.why: `document.cookie` is redefined to throw on get and set, and the sidebar still toggles to `collapsed` — the `document.cookie` clause.

citations.anchor: falls back to desktop when matchMedia is unavailable
citations.why: `window.matchMedia` is deleted and rendering must not throw — the `matchMedia` environment-check clause.

citations.anchor: reflects a chosen theme onto <html>
citations.why: Asserts both mechanisms in one case: `documentElement.classList.contains('dark')` and `documentElement.style.colorScheme === 'dark'`.

citations.anchor: falls back to a working no-op outside a provider
citations.why: Renders the `useAppearance` probe with no `AppearanceProvider`: theme is `system`, resolved is `light`, and calling `setTheme` does not throw.

citations.anchor: hoists itself into the inset strip, above the scrollport
citations.why: Asserts the `top-bar` node's `parentElement` is the `sidebar-inset-bar` strip, so inside an inset it renders only through the portal; the second clause — that a `null` host draws nothing at all — has no case (the spec covers `undefined`, i.e. no inset, instead).

citations.anchor: dismisses only the toast whose body was clicked
citations.why: Three toasts are raised, the second's body is clicked, and only the second is marked removed — the first clause exactly.

citations.anchor: lets the close button own its own click
citations.why: Clicking `[data-close-button]` removes exactly one toast rather than being swallowed by the wrapper handler. The link clause has its own case — "leaves a link inside the toast to navigate" — which clicks an `<a>` inside a toast body and asserts the toast survives; dropping `a` from `toastBodyOf`'s escape list fails it. The action/cancel clause is recorded `partial`: sonner dismisses on both anyway, so the wrapper intercepting and standing aside are indistinguishable through any observable this harness has.

citations.anchor: nothing opts out of the user palette
citations.why: Under `forcedColors: 'active'`, counts every element whose computed `forcedColorAdjust === 'none'` and asserts zero — the second clause exactly.

citations.anchor: a button keeps a visible focus indicator
citations.why: Under `forcedColors: 'active'` asserts the ring's `box-shadow` really is discarded and the focused button still resolves a non-`none` outline ≥1px — which is the single global `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid !important }` rule in the library's styles.css, so removing it fails here; the sampling is two elements (a button and, in the next case, the scrollport), not 'every' focusable.

citations.anchor: renders every step when two share a label
citations.why: Three steps, two sharing the label 'Details': asserts all three buttons render, both hints are present, and React logged no 'same key' warning — a caption-keyed list fails.

citations.anchor: keeps two options with the same label independently chosen
citations.why: Two options sharing the label 'Posts' with distinct values yield `aria-checked` `['false','true']`, so the rows did not merge; the sibling case pins that only one of the two is highlighted.

citations.anchor: finds an option by searching its value as well as its label
citations.why: Typing `media:` filters to the option whose value (not label) matches — the `keywords` half of the invariant.

design-system:I-10.missing: The "two mounted at once is a defect" clause, which is about a *page* and not about any component here. The library half is fully pinned: each shipped loading surface (`SkeletonRegion` over six placeholders, `AppLoader`, `WizardPageSkeleton` over ~29) exposes exactly one `role="status"`, counted with `{ hidden: true }` so a role that crept back onto a placeholder inside the region's `aria-hidden` wrapper is still seen. Re-checked for a defence that could be unit-tested and there is none by design: nesting one `SkeletonRegion` in another yields two regions, because a surface cannot know what its page mounts beside it. The clause therefore needs a route held in its loading state and a count of live regions on the whole document — an `admin-e2e` assertion (delay the route's `/api` mock, then `expect(page.getByRole('status')).toHaveCount(1)`), not a jsdom render.

design-system:I-33.missing: The "status dots are always accompanied by text" clause, which is about no component in this package. The two clauses that are about this library are pinned (`state-affordances.spec.tsx`: the selected `SegmentedControlItem` pairs `data-[state=on]:bg-primary` with `data-[state=on]:font-semibold`, and the active `SidebarMenuButton` pairs `data-[active=true]:bg-sidebar-accent` with `data-[active=true]:font-medium`). Re-checked the tree: the library ships no status-dot primitive at all, and the two that exist are consumers' — `workspaces-admin`'s `StatusChip` and `users-admin`'s `MemberStatusBadge`, each an `aria-hidden` `size-1.5 rounded-full` span beside its own label, and neither has a spec. The clause is theirs to pin, either in those two packages or as an `admin-e2e` scan over rendered pages; a scan written here would cache against their source trees and live in the wrong package.
